claim.pdf_says: 6)  **General case mappings.** The following case mappings have been added.   [printed as ordinary numbered list item 6) of clause E.3.3]
claim.markdown_says: ## 6) **General case mappings.** The following case mappings have been added.   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49521)
claim.why_it_matters: Same defect as item 5) on page 1213: a numbered list item inside E.3.3 promoted to a level-2 markdown heading, creating a phantom top-level section in the outline that has no counterpart in the standard.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on both sides, and the claim is quoted accurately.

PDF (rendered E:/Temp/specrecon/v1222/spec_p1222.png at 300dpi, printed page number 1192): at roughly two-thirds down the page, immediately after the 'Zanabazar_Square: 11A00-11A3E, 11A47' block and immediately before the parenthesised case-mapping pair listing, the page prints a hanging-indent numbered list item. The glyphs I see are: the numeral '6' followed by a right parenthesis ')' at the outer list margin, then whitespace, then 'General case mappings.' in bold body serif, then 'The following case mappings have been added.' in regular body serif on the same line. Its left margin, hanging indent, body-serif face and bold lead-in are identical to items 1) through 4) printed under E.3.3 on page 1212 and to items 7) onward later in the same list. It carries no clause number, no heading font, no heading whitespace, and no larger type size. It is unambiguously an ordinary list item, not a heading.

Markdown: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49521 reads exactly '## 6) **General case mappings.** The following case mappings have been added.' — verified in the raw file with cat -A, so the leading '## ' is literal ATX heading markup and not an artifact of the page slice.

The difference is not reflow, wrapping, hyphenation or page-break furniture: the prose text is byte-identical between the two, and the sole difference is the injected '## ' prefix. It is a genuine markup-level discrepancy that changes document structure rather than wording.

The structural harm is confirmed by the surrounding outline. In specs/ISO_COBOL.md, '## ' is the level used for real clause headings in this region — '## Annex E' (48516), '## E.3 Substantive changes probably not affecting existing programs' (48904), '## E.3.3 Not affecting' (48946), '## Annex F' (49824) — as well as for the injected page markers. Promoting list item 6) to '## ' makes it a structural peer of clause E.3.3 itself, i.e. a phantom section with no counterpart in ISO/IEC 1989:2023, and it visually terminates the E.3.3 list even though the list demonstrably continues (items 7) through 36)+ follow later, all correctly rendered as plain paragraphs).

The claim's characterisation as the same defect as item 5) also checks out: line 48984 is '## 5) **Characters permitted in user-defined words.** The following characters have been added.' Items 1)-4) (lines 48948-48956) and 7)+ in the very same numbered list are correctly plain paragraphs of the form 'N) **Lead-in.** text', so 5) and 6) are the only two anomalies — and both are exactly the two items whose bodies are followed by long block listings, which is the likely OCR/conversion trigger.

One caveat worth recording, since severity was asserted rather than derived: no prose content is lost or altered. This is purely a markup/outline defect. Any consumer reading the file linearly still gets the correct text; only outline extraction, section-anchor generation, and any tooling that treats '## ' as a clause boundary are affected.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed; no correction to the substance. Refinements for the ledger: (1) PDF page 1222 is printed page 1192 of the standard, and item 6) sits under clause E.3.3 'Not affecting' inside Annex E. (2) No text is lost or altered — the prose is byte-identical on both sides and the entire defect is the injected '## ' prefix, so this is a markup/outline corruption rather than a content discrepancy; 'structural' is the right severity but the finding should not be read as missing text. (3) The phantom heading is a structural peer of the real '## E.3.3 Not affecting' heading (line 48946) and of '## Annex E' (line 48516), and it prematurely terminates the E.3.3 numbered list even though items 7) through 36)+ continue after it. (4) Within that same list, items 1)-4) (lines 48948-48956) and 7) onward are correctly rendered as plain 'N) **Lead-in.** text' paragraphs, so items 5) (line 48984) and 6) (line 49521) are the only two promoted — and they are precisely the two items whose bodies are followed by long block listings of code-point data, which is the probable conversion trigger. Fix for both: strip the leading '## ' so line 49521 reads '6) **General case mappings.** The following case mappings have been added.'
